area.title: Character & greeting
area.description: Iris's personality, the daily greeting and the context she greets with.

epic.title: Daily greeting, weather-aware
epic.body: Once a day, the first time the owner is at the Mac, Iris greets him with one spoken sentence that uses the weather facts she already has (context/weather.py), then stays quiet. Never twice a day, never when muted, never during a meeting or screen share. The definition lists this under Personality and it is one of the three spoken moments.

epic.title: Greeting context contract shared by memory and the greeting expert
epic.body: Define one event shape, greeting_context, that the memory store publishes and the greeting expert consumes: the fields (last greeted local date, the weather facts used, whether the owner was on a call or muted), who writes it, who reads it, and where it is persisted. Both the memory charter and the experts charter currently describe this differently (experts/memory.py sits under experts by path prefix but the experts charter says it belongs to memory), so the two must agree on the same shape and the map must say who owns experts/memory.py. Mac only.

area.title: Mac & mobile apps
area.description: The desktop app and phone apps, and the errands that run between them.

epic.title: Phone→Mac errand flow
epic.body: The owner states an errand on the phone ("tidy my Chrome tabs", "make me a doc about X"); it runs on the Mac through the cloud agent when the Mac is awake, is queued durably when it is not, and the result comes back to the phone, with one spoken sentence on the Mac when it lands. Machine-bound tasks run on the Mac; portable tasks (documents, answers) run in iris-api with the laptop shut. Road doc move 2: every task carries a locality.
